It also discloses that a 429 now stops the drain at its first job.

criteria.criterion: The diff limits itself to the deliverables: no status display, no new record kind and no change to retry or resume logic (the resumable_stop and keeps_unfinished_work behaviour is unchanged). Checked with `git diff --stat`.

No record or data file, display.rs or status code changed.

findings.summary: The doc comment on usage_limit_hit says only a success or error subtype counts, but the code also accepts a detail with no subtype prefix.
findings.evidence: `.find_map(|subtype| detail.strip_prefix(subtype)).unwrap_or(detail)` falls back to the whole detail, and the test 'you've hit your weekly limit - resets: Nov 12' (no prefix) is accepted. Prefixed other subtypes are still refused, because the text then starts 'error_max_turns:'. So the behaviour is safe, but the documented rule and the code differ. Either refuse unprefixed details or state the fallback in the comment.

findings.summary: The `drain --help` line for 'usage limit' names only weekly and session limits, though a 429 now also ends the drain with Stop::UsageLimit.
findings.evidence: The help says "a job's reply said the weekly or session usage limit was reached", while the Stop::UsageLimit doc and the CHANGELOG say the stop covers a 429 too.

findings.summary: A test comment still lists usage limit among the causes of the fail-twice stop.
findings.evidence: The comment says "Only a cause that every later item would share (login, usage limit, disk) ends the run". A usage limit now ends the run at its first job through Stop::UsageLimit, not after two failures.

summary: The change does what was asked. `usage_limit_hit` in claude.rs recognises a 'You've hit your weekly/session limit … resets <time>' reply, but only at the start of the text under the success or error subtype. The existing disk.rs path (`producer_stop_reason`, `StopCause::of`) now closes such a job with the USAGE_LIMIT environment reason and keeps the reset time in it, and `usage_limit_reset` reads the time back. The drain stops at the first such job with the new stop 'usage limit' and a note giving the reset time. I ran the targeted tests myself and all passed: `cargo test -p athena-agent usage_limit` in the normal debug build, and the core, CLI and control tests with `--release`. I used `--release` because the debug build of athena-core in the shared target directory picked up a stale athena-agent artifact and failed to compile (unresolved `usage_limit_hit`). That is a build-cache problem, not a fault in the candidate: CI passed fmt, clippy and the full test suite for this commit, and Athena's policy blocked `cargo --config`, so I did not force a debug rebuild. Only expected files changed; retry and resume functions, the record kinds and the status display are untouched. Findings are minor: a doc comment says more than the code enforces, the help line for 'usage limit' omits the 429 case, and one test comment is stale.
